DataMEDS AI experienced a significant rise of 87.20%, closing at $1.62. The stock’s intraday high was $3.85, with a low of $0.87, and a 52-week range of $3.88 to $0.82. In after-hours trading, the stock shot up 17.9% to $1.91.

This acquisition aims to expand DataMEDS’ services into cancer management.
Trip.com Group stock rose by 0.44%, closing at $39.25. The stock reached an intraday high of $40.14 and a low of $39.08, with a 52-week high of $78.99 and a low of $38.04.

Trip.com Group reported second-quarter revenue of RMB15.7 billion ($2.3 billion), up 6% year over year, while non-GAAP EPS rose to RMB7.27 ($1.07) from RMB7.20 a year earlier. International platform revenue grew more than 50%, while the company posted a RMB2.4 billion ($361 million) net loss largely due to a RMB5.2 billion ($763 million) anti-monopoly penalty; excluding the penalty, net income was RMB2.7 billion ($402 million).

Datavault AI saw its stock drop by 18.24%, closing at $0.16. The stock’s intraday high was $0.19, with a low of $0.15, and a 52-week range of $4.10 to $0.15. In the after-hours session, the shares rose 1.08% to $0.16.

Datavault AI received an initial $100 million purchase order for its QEST tokenization services, opening its Information Data Exchange, NILvault and American Political Exchange platforms. The company reaffirmed its 2026 revenue guidance of $200 million, while ongoing securities litigation continued to create uncertainty around the commercial milestone.

Circle Internet Group experienced a decline of 11.41%, closing at $86.30. The stock hit an intraday high of $93.29 and a low of $84.80, with a 52-week high of $159.47 and a low of $49.90. In after-hours trading, the stock fell 1.87% to $84.69.

(CRYPTO: USDC)-issuer’s stock fell after the Senate’s CLARITY Act cloture vote fell short of the 60-vote threshold, with 41 senators voting against advancing the bill, including several Democratic senators who had participated in negotiations.
